trajectory_summary: The call opens warm and cooperative, dips into mild suspicion when the customer questions the 'deal' and a mysterious prior text, then resolves once the bill photo is received and scheduling proceeds smoothly. Outcome is a booked phone appointment for a specific day and time, though button-up is thin on the required elements.

observed_outcome.quote: K. We'll call you tomorrow at 2PM, and I'll text you after this to remind you. Okay?
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow) and time (2PM) were agreed and confirmed by the customer, meeting the booked bar; the wife identified as co-owner was never invited onto the appointment.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: Rep acknowledged the $700 bill generically at 01:03 ('We can definitely help lower that') but never tied it back explicitly when booking or discussing the appointment — the flip should have landed around 06:11 when confirming the appointment, reinforcing that the specialist call is specifically about bringing that bill down.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: Are you able to access the power bill real quick?
bill_document_audit.reasoning: Rep asked for the bill early; customer agreed to send a picture and later sent it during the call, and the rep confirmed receipt at 06:11.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep did not ask what specifically motivated the customer to pursue solar.

objections.reasoning: Rep over-explained mechanics (scope creep) but it satisfied the customer, who then agreed to send the bill photo.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Setter scope creep on pricing/mechanism questions
primary_coaching_focus.quote: We got cool programs where it's called the bill swap. We look at your power bill, and we remove it, and then we replace it with a lower and cheaper solar bill.
primary_coaching_focus.why: Rep explained the full bill-swap value prop and no-upfront-cost claim instead of bridging to the specialist, giving away appointment value and creating room for future scrutiny.

key_moments.quote: It depends if you it just depends on what route you wanna go.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep answers a pricing/mechanism question with a detailed bill-swap and no-upfront-cost explanation instead of bridging to the specialist.

key_moments.quote: Oh, you're gonna have my text?
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer references a prior text the rep denies sending, a legitimacy flag that is brushed past instead of clarified.
A $700 high-season bill is a strong anchor point but the rep only briefly acknowledges it generically.
